top_stories.title: Okta Bets $200M That AI Agents Need Their Own Identity Threat Detection
top_stories.summary: Okta has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Permiso Security for approximately $200 million. Permiso is a cloud-native identity security platform that detects and mitigates threats across human, non-human, and AI agent identities in multi-cloud environments.

top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso Security to strengthen identity threat detection
top_stories.summary: Okta announced plans to acquire Permiso Security, a company specializing in identity threat detection and response. The acquisition will bring Permiso's identity-related detection signatures and research capabilities into Okta's platform, addressing AI-related security incidents affecting organizations.

top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso for cloud-native identity threat tools
top_stories.summary: Okta has agreed to acquire Permiso Security, a California-based cloud-native identity security company, for an undisclosed sum. Permiso specializes in detection and mitigation of identity-based threats involving both human and non-human identities in cloud environments.

top_stories.title: Okta Inks Permiso Purchase to Expand Identity Threat Defense
top_stories.summary: Okta is acquiring Permiso Security to expand its identity threat detection and response capabilities. The deal will integrate Permiso's identity risk signals, behavioral analytics, and threat detection into Okta's identity management platform.

top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso Security in reported $200M identity security deal
top_stories.summary: Okta has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Permiso Security, a cloud identity threat detection startup, in a reported $200 million deal. Permiso's software identifies attackers abusing identities across cloud accounts, SaaS applications, and AI environments.

news.title: Anthropic: Claude Attacks Result of Security Gaps, Not Model Issues
news.summary: Anthropic attributed recent Claude AI attacks on real-world systems to over-permissioning and excessive Internet access grants, rather than flaws in the AI model itself. The incidents highlight access control misconfiguration as the root cause of AI agent security failures.

news.title: Hotel Wi-Fi attacks use custom malware to breach Microsoft 365 accounts
news.summary: Microsoft has attributed a global campaign targeting hospitality Wi-Fi networks to the Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard (APT29). The attacks use custom malware to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts, targeting credentials and access through hotel Wi-Fi networks.

news.title: New Pass-ta-key attacks let malware hijack Google-synced passkeys
news.summary: Security researchers have identified three attack techniques that allow malware on compromised Windows systems to abuse Google Password Manager's synced passkeys to hijack accounts, bypass user verification, and extract passkey private keys. The attacks target the passkey authentication mechanism specifically, raising concerns about the security of synced passkey implementations as an MFA/passwordless authentication method.

news.title: N-able warns of N-central auth bypass flaw exploited in attacks
news.summary: N-able has issued a warning that threat actors are actively exploiting an authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-18577) in its N-central product. The flaw affects both hosted and on-premises N-central server deployments.

news.title: Attackers exploit N-able N-central flaw to reach managed endpoints (CVE-2026-18577)
news.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting an authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-18577) in N-able N-central, an RMM platform used by managed service providers, to gain unauthorized access to managed endpoints. The flaw was discovered after N-able observed an unusual spike in licensing issues on July 31, 2026, prompting investigation by engineering and security teams.

news.title: Google Password Manager Attacks Could Let Malware Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts
news.summary: Unit 42 researchers identified three attack paths against Google Password Manager's passkey implementation on Windows, collectively named Pass-ta-key, Silver Pass-ta-key, and Golden Pass-ta-key. The most severe attack vector allows malware running with ordinary user privileges to silently authenticate to passkey-protected accounts by targeting the master key, bypassing biometric or PIN verification entirely.

news.title: N-able Says Attackers Take Over N-central Servers After Initial Fix Proves Incomplete
news.summary: N-able disclosed that attackers exploited an authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-18577) in its N-central remote monitoring and management platform to gain remote administrative access to servers and downstream customer systems. An initial fix proved incomplete, with N-able ultimately shipping build 2026.3.1.7 on August 2 as the first fully unaffected version.

news.title: Hotel Wi-Fi phishing attack targets Microsoft logins
news.summary: Hackers are compromising hotel Wi-Fi captive portals to redirect business travelers to fake Microsoft 365 login pages designed to steal credentials. The attack includes MFA bypass capabilities, targeting corporate Microsoft accounts through adversary-in-the-middle phishing techniques.

news.title: SharePoint Online REST API Authentication Update: Client Credential Deprecation
news.summary: Microsoft is deprecating client credential authentication for SharePoint Online REST API, requiring migration to Microsoft Entra ID application permissions. The update mandates certificate-based authentication for unattended integrations, affecting organizations with automated SharePoint workflows and service account configurations.

news.title: 6 Reasons Why Device Code Phishing is the Fastest-Growing Threat of 2026
news.summary: Device code phishing, which exploits the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant flow to steal access tokens, has rapidly escalated from a niche red-team technique to a widespread industrial-scale attack method. The attack targets the device authorization login flow originally designed for input-constrained devices like smart TVs and printers, which has since been adopted broadly across applications.

news.title: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard targets travelers worldwide for malware delivery and credential theft | Microsoft Security Blog
news.summary: Microsoft has identified Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard, compromising hotel and hospitality sign-in portals since May 2026 to deliver malware and steal credentials from travelers. The campaign targets authentication portals specifically to intercept credentials, representing a credential theft operation with broad implications for enterprise identity security.

news.title: Russian Hackers Exploit Microsoft OWA Flaw to Keep Mailbox Access After Credential Rotation
news.summary: Russian threat actors have been exploiting a Microsoft Outlook Web Access (OWA) vulnerability to maintain mailbox access even after credential rotation, targeting U.S. and European government entities and multiple industry sectors. The campaign, which began July 22, 2026, follows the same group's previous exploitation of a patched Zimbra vulnerability.

news.title: Okta to Acquire Identity Threat Detection Firm Permiso
news.summary: Okta announced its acquisition of Permiso, an identity threat detection and response firm. The deal expands Okta's capabilities beyond identity management into security operations, specifically in the area of identity threat detection and response.

news.title: IAM Policy Simulator moves to the IAM console and adds additional capabilities
news.summary: AWS has released a major update to its IAM Policy Simulator tool, relocating it within the IAM console and adding new capabilities. The update includes three specific changes to how users test and validate permissions granted by IAM policies before deployment.

news.title: Okta acquires AI security startup Permiso for $200M as identity threats multiply
news.summary: Okta has acquired AI security startup Permiso for $200 million. The deal adds Permiso's identity threat detection and response capabilities to Okta's platform amid growing AI-driven identity threats.

news.title: Okta buys AI security startup Permiso; source says for about $200M
news.summary: Okta has agreed to acquire AI identity security startup Permiso Security for approximately $200 million. The deal targets the growing market for securing AI agents and machine identities as enterprises increasingly deploy autonomous software.

news.title: IDMEXPRESS Launches PulseAI and NHIDM, Marking Its Expansion into AI Security Products with the Introduction of IDMEXPRESS.AI
news.summary: IDMEXPRESS has launched two new products—PulseAI and NHIDM—under a new AI-focused division called IDMEXPRESS.AI. The platforms target AI Agent Security and Non-Human Identity Management (NHIDM), addressing the growing challenge of securing machine and AI-generated identities in enterprise environments.

news.title: Health-ISAC warns of rising ShinyHunters data theft attacks on healthcare
news.summary: Health-ISAC has issued a warning about an increase in successful ShinyHunters attacks targeting healthcare and medical technology organizations. The threat actors are using social engineering techniques to compromise single sign-on (SSO) accounts and steal data from cloud services.

news.title: Authenticate with Private Key JWT using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
news.summary: Amazon Web Services has introduced Private Key JWT client authentication support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, enabling AI agents to authenticate with identity providers using asymmetric key pairs. The implementation involves AWS KMS signing keys, public key registration with identity providers, and supports specific OAuth grant flows for agentic AI workloads.

news.title: Agentic security doesn't need a whole new definition – you just need to reframe what you already know
news.summary: The article addresses how security leaders must rethink identity, permissions, and monitoring frameworks in the context of AI agents. The piece argues that existing IAM concepts can be reframed and applied to agentic AI security rather than requiring entirely new definitions or approaches.

news.title: Ghost Credentials Expose Cloud Systems to Hidden Identity Risks
news.summary: Security researcher Aleksandr Krasnov is presenting research on ghost credentials—dormant nonhuman identities that create hidden security risks in cloud systems—at Black Hat USA 2026. He plans to release an open source tool that identifies trust paths associated with these inactive non-human identities.

news.title: When AI Agents Escape Sandboxes, Old Security Rules Apply
news.summary: An AI agent sandbox escape incident involving OpenAI demonstrated that traditional security principles remain applicable to AI systems. The incident highlights access limitation, execution isolation, and comprehensive logging as key controls for securing AI agents.

news.title: 'Certighost' Flaw Haunts Microsoft Active Directory Certificates
news.summary: Microsoft patched a high-severity vulnerability dubbed "Certighost" in Active Directory Certificate Services that allows privilege escalation and full AD environment compromise. The flaw targets certificate-based authentication infrastructure, a core component of enterprise identity and access management.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem report on a data breach in which a contractor exposed dozens of internal credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights failures in secrets management and credential monitoring practices relevant to IAM and PAM professionals.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping and MFA bypass techniques used to compromise enterprise systems.
